subject: physics
title: Energy dissipation
key_idea: Energy can be transferred usefully, stored or **dissipated**, but never created or destroyed. In every system change, some energy is dissipated into less useful stores. This is usually the thermal store of the surroundings, and it is often called wasted energy.

blocks.text: Not all the energy in a system change ends up where you want it. This section covers what happens to the rest.

items.meaning: Energy transferred to the store or form you want, such as the kinetic store of a moving car.
Energy stored in less useful ways, so it spreads out and cannot be used again. Often called 'wasted'.
Always the same before and after. Dissipating energy does not destroy it.

items: A gas boiler: the chemical store of the fuel decreases. The thermal store of the water increases, and the thermal store of the air increases too.
A car engine: the chemical store of the fuel decreases. The kinetic store of the car increases and the thermal store of the engine and surroundings increases.
A bouncing ball: some energy goes to the thermal store of the ball, the floor and the air, and some to sound.

diagram.alt: Sort each energy transfer into useful or wasted.
diagram.prompt: Is this transfer useful or wasted?

items.text: Thermal store of the water in a kettle
Thermal store of the kettle's surroundings
Kinetic store of a moving car
Thermal store of a car's brakes and engine
Thermal energy from a lamp's bulb
Gravitational potential store of a lifted load
Thermal store of a crane's motor and cable

items: Energy is transferred usefully, stored or dissipated. It is never created or destroyed.
Dissipated energy is stored in less useful ways, usually as thermal energy in the surroundings.
The total energy before and after is the same.

blocks.text: Most wasted energy comes from friction, air resistance and electrical resistance. Each makes the surroundings warmer.

items: **Friction.** Work done against friction raises the temperature. Wheels rubbing on an axle make it warm.
**Air resistance.** A moving object does work against drag. A swinging pendulum loses height after each swing.
**Electrical resistance.** Resistance in wires and motor coils transfers energy to thermal energy.

blocks.text: A mechanical process becomes wasteful when it causes a rise in temperature. The energy is dissipated by heating the surroundings.

items.text: A car rolls down a hill with its engine off. It starts with energy in its gravitational potential store.
Some of that energy is transferred to the kinetic store.
Work is done against friction and drag. Energy is transferred to the thermal energy store of the surroundings.
The kinetic energy at the bottom is less than the potential energy at the top.

items: Friction, air resistance and electrical resistance all dissipate energy by heating.
A braking vehicle transfers kinetic energy to the thermal store of the brakes and surroundings.
Dissipated energy is no longer available to do anything useful.

sections.heading: Explaining energy loss in an exam

blocks.text: A good answer names the stores and says where the energy goes.

items: Say that energy is dissipated, or transferred to the surroundings.
Name the store that increases: thermal, or sound.
Link to the cause: friction, air resistance or resistance in wires.
Do not say that energy is used up or destroyed.
Say what happens to the energy: it is dissipated to the surroundings as thermal energy.
Name the cause: friction, drag or resistance.
Never say energy is lost from the universe.

checks.q: A cyclist uses the brakes to stop. Explain what happens to the kinetic energy of the cyclist.
checks.a: The kinetic energy store decreases to zero. The energy is dissipated, transferred to the thermal energy store of the brakes and surroundings.

checks.q: Explain why the axles of a cart become warm when the wheels turn.
checks.a: Friction between the wheel and the axle causes heating, so energy is transferred to the thermal store.

checks.q: State what happens to the total energy when some energy is dissipated.
checks.a: The total energy stays the same. The energy is stored in less useful ways.

exam_phrases: chemical energy store of the fuel decreases
thermal energy store of the water increases
thermal energy store of the air / atmosphere increases
so more energy is usefully transferred

mistakes.wrong: The boiler heats the water, so the water gains energy.
mistakes.right: Name the stores and say what happens: the chemical store of the fuel decreases and the thermal store of the water and the air increases.

mistakes.wrong: Lubricating the skateboard reduces the friction between the wheels and the ramp.
mistakes.right: That is not accepted. Say it reduces the amount of friction, so more energy is usefully transferred and there is a greater kinetic energy.

mistakes.wrong: Oiling a wind turbine means more electricity is generated.
mistakes.right: That is ignored. Say the efficiency increases because less energy is wasted by friction.

worked_example.question:
A gas boiler is used to heat a house.

Describe how different energy stores are changed by the boiler.
answer_points: The chemical energy store of the fuel decreases
The thermal energy store of the water increases
The thermal energy store of the air / atmosphere increases
worked_example.tip: A kinetic energy store of the water or air particles increasing is also allowed for the last two marks.

exam_phrases: the kinetic energy (store) / it decreases (to zero)
friction (between the wheel and the axle)

mistakes.wrong: The ball does not bounce back up because it runs out of energy.
mistakes.right: Say the ball has lost energy, then say where it went: dissipated, transferred to the surroundings as thermal energy, or sound.

mistakes.wrong: The axles are warm because the wheels are electrical.
mistakes.right: The wheel rubs on the axle. Friction causes heating, so energy is transferred to the thermal store.

mistakes.wrong: When the cyclist brakes, the kinetic energy disappears.
mistakes.right: The kinetic energy store decreases to zero. The energy is dissipated and the thermal energy store of the brakes and surroundings increases.

worked_example.question:
A cyclist has a mass of 64 kg.
The cyclist uses the brakes on the bicycle to stop.

Explain what happens to the kinetic energy of the cyclist.
answer_points: The energy is dissipated, or transferred to the surroundings
The thermal energy (store) increases (for example the brake pads become hot)
worked_example.tip: Any two of these linked ideas score the 2 marks.

exam_phrases: energy is transferred to the thermal energy (store)
(work is done against) friction / drag / resistive forces
energy is transferred in the surroundings
energy transferred to the surroundings by heating

mistakes.wrong: The pendulum bob loses energy, so it swings lower.
mistakes.right: Pendulum loses energy is ignored. Say friction or air resistance does work on the pendulum and energy is transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings.

mistakes.wrong: The kinetic energy decreases, so the maximum height decreases.
mistakes.right: That is ignored. Give a cause: friction, air resistance or drag, and where the energy goes.

mistakes.wrong: The kinetic energy at the bottom of the hill is less because friction occurs.
mistakes.right: Also say where the energy goes: it is transferred to the thermal energy store, or to the surroundings by heating.

worked_example.question:
A car with a mass of 800 kg rolls down a hill with its engine switched off.

The kinetic energy at the bottom of the hill is less than the potential energy at the top of the hill.

Explain why.
Write about energy stores.
answer_points: Energy is transferred to the thermal energy (store)
And any one of: work is done against friction / drag / resistive forces, or energy is transferred in the surroundings / brakes
worked_example.tip: Heat is allowed for thermal energy. Energy transferred to the surroundings by heating scores both marks.
